def-nufft-finite-array-norms:
## Definition

For a finite index set $E$ and a complex array $z=(z_e)_{e\in E}$, define
$$\|z\|_1=\sum_{e\in E}|z_e|,\qquad \|z\|_2=\left(\sum_{e\in E}|z_e|^2\right)^{1/2},\qquad \|z\|_\infty=\max_{e\in E}|z_e|.$$
For $z,w\in\mathbb C^E$, define the counting inner product by $\langle z,w\rangle_E=\sum_{e\in E}z_e\overline{w_e}$. By [[lem-complex-conjugation-and-modulus-laws]], $\langle z,z\rangle_E=\sum_{e\in E}|z_e|^2$, so $\|z\|_2=\sqrt{\langle z,z\rangle_E}$. For $E=\varnothing$, all three norms and this inner product are defined to be zero. For nonempty finite $E$, the maximum exists by repeated comparison in the real order. Complex modulus is as in [[def-intervals-rectangles-and-complex-balls]], conjugation as in [[def-complex-conjugate-real-imaginary-part-and-modulus]], finite sums as in [[def-finite-sum-in-a-commutative-monoid]], and the square root is the unique nonnegative root.
def-nufft-periodized-gaussian-gridding-k:
## Definition

For a real parameter $\tau>0$, define the period-one Gaussian gridding kernel by the series

$$\phi_\tau(x)=\sum_{n\in\mathbb Z}\exp\!\left(-\frac{\pi(x+n)^2}{\tau}\right),\qquad x\in\mathbb R.$$

The series is the formal periodization; [[lem-nufft-gaussian-periodization-converges]] proves that it converges absolutely and locally uniformly, so its value is a continuous one-periodic real function. Its Fourier coefficient at $r\in\mathbb Z$ is denoted $\widehat\phi_\tau(r)=\int_0^1\phi_\tau(x)e^{-2\pi i r x}\,dx$ when this integral is used; [[lem-nufft-gaussian-periodization-fourier-series]] computes it exactly. The kernel is nonnegative and satisfies $\phi_\tau(x+1)=\phi_\tau(x)$.
lem-nufft-finite-euclidean-norm-triangle:
## Statement

For a finite index set $E$ and arrays $x,y\in\mathbb C^E$, the Euclidean norm of [[def-nufft-finite-array-norms]] satisfies
$$\|x+y\|_2\le\|x\|_2+\|y\|_2.$$
def-nufft-transform-types-and-mode-conve:
## Definition

Fix an integer dimension $d\ge1$. Let $\mathbb T^d=[0,1)^d$ be the chosen representatives for period-one coordinates; all coordinates in a type-1 or type-2 transform are interpreted modulo integer shifts. Here $\pi$ is the real constant defined in [[def-real-elementary-functions-and-domains]]. For $x\in\mathbb R^d$ and $k\in\mathbb Z^d$, write $k\cdot x=\sum_{r=1}^d k_rx_r$. Let $N,J\ge0$ be finite integers, let $x_0,\ldots,x_{N-1}\in\mathbb T^d$, let $c=(c_j)_{j<N}\in\mathbb C^N$, and choose integers $K_r\ge0$. The rectangular mode set is

$$\mathcal K=\prod_{r=1}^d\{-K_r,-K_r+1,\ldots,K_r\}.$$

The **type-1 nonuniform discrete Fourier transform** maps source coefficients to integer-mode samples:

$$F_k=\sum_{j=0}^{N-1}c_j e^{-2\pi i k\cdot x_j},\qquad k\in\mathcal K.$$

The **type-2 nonuniform discrete Fourier transform** maps a coefficient array $(f_k)_{k\in\mathcal K}$ to values at the same point list:

$$g_j=\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}f_k e^{+2\pi i k\cdot x_j},\qquad 0\le j<N.$$

For the type-1 matrix $A=(e^{-2\pi i k\cdot x_j})_{k\in\mathcal K,\,j<N}$, define its conjugate transpose by $(A^*)_{jk}=\overline{A_{kj}}$. Use the finite counting inner products from [[def-nufft-finite-array-norms]]; the type-2 matrix is $A^*$ as proved below.

The **type-3 nonuniform discrete Fourier transform** takes a finite source list $x_0,\ldots,x_{N-1}\in\mathbb R^d$, coefficients $c_j\in\mathbb C$, and a separately specified finite frequency list $\xi_0,\ldots,\xi_{J-1}\in\mathbb R^d$, and returns

$$G_\ell=\sum_{j=0}^{N-1}c_j e^{-2\pi i \xi_\ell\cdot x_j},\qquad 0\le\ell<J.$$

Type 3 has no integer-mode restriction or implicit coordinate wrapping. No frequency normalization, axis scaling, or frequency-space product is implicit; any such scaling is separate input data whose cost must be analyzed separately. Each displayed map is a finite sum of defined complex exponentials; the zero-source case has the empty-sum value zero and the zero-output case returns the empty array. No fast algorithm or complexity claim for type 3 is part of this definition.
lem-nufft-gaussian-periodization-converg:
## Statement
For every $\tau>0$, the series defining $\phi_\tau(x)$ converges absolutely and uniformly on each compact interval of $x$. Its sum is continuous on $\mathbb R$ and has period one.
lem-nufft-gaussian-image-tail-bound:
## Statement
For $\tau>0$, integer $L\ge1$, and $x\in[0,1]$, put
$$\phi_{\tau,L}(x)=\sum_{n=-L}^{L}\exp\!\left(-\frac{\pi(x+n)^2}{\tau}\right),\qquad R_{\tau,L}=\frac{2\exp(-\pi L^2/\tau)}{1-\exp(-\pi L/\tau)}.$$
Then $0\le\phi_\tau(x)-\phi_{\tau,L}(x)\le R_{\tau,L}$, and the denominator defining $R_{\tau,L}$ is positive.
lem-nufft-gaussian-periodization-fourier:
## Statement
Assume Countable Choice. For $\tau>0$, the Fourier coefficient of $\phi_\tau$ at each integer $r$ is $\widehat\phi_\tau(r)=\sqrt{\tau}\exp(-\pi\tau r^2)$, and
$$\phi_\tau(x)=\sum_{r\in\mathbb Z}\sqrt{\tau}\exp(-\pi\tau r^2)e^{2\pi i r x}.$$
The periodized series on the left converges locally uniformly, and the Fourier series on the right converges absolutely and uniformly.
lem-nufft-gaussian-spread-truncation-tai:
## Statement
Let $d\ge1$, $\tau_r>0$, and integers $M_r,w_r\ge1$ satisfy $M_r\ge2w_r+1$. Define $a_r=\pi/(\tau_rM_r^2)$ and
$$S_r=\frac{2}{1-\exp(-a_r)},\qquad T_r=2\exp(-a_rw_r^2)\left(1+\frac{1}{2a_rw_r}\right).$$
For $x=(x_r)_{r=1}^d\in[0,1)^d$, let
$$W_r(x_r)=\left\{\ell\in\{0,\ldots,M_r-1\}:\min_{n\in\mathbb Z}|\ell/M_r-x_r-n|\le w_r/M_r\right\},\quad W(x)=\prod_{r=1}^dW_r(x_r).$$
With $\Phi_\tau(z)=\prod_{r=1}^d\phi_{\tau_r}(z_r)$, the omitted spreading mass obeys
$$\sum_{\ell\in\prod_r\{0,\ldots,M_r-1\}\setminus W(x)}\Phi_\tau(\ell_1/M_1-x_1,\ldots,\ell_d/M_d-x_d)\le T_d,\qquad T_d:=\sum_{r=1}^dT_r\prod_{s\ne r}S_s.$$
Also $\sum_{\ell_r=0}^{M_r-1}\phi_{\tau_r}(\ell_r/M_r-x_r)\le S_r$ for every coordinate and point.
lem-nufft-gaussian-grid-alias-identity-a:
## Statement
Assume Countable Choice. Let $d\ge1$, $N\ge0$, $c_j\in\mathbb C$, $x_j\in[0,1)^d$, integers $K_r\ge0$, positive integers $M_r>2K_r$, and $\tau_r>0$. Write $P=\prod_{r=1}^dM_r$, define $\Phi_\tau(z)=\prod_{r=1}^d\phi_{\tau_r}(z_r)$, and let
$$g_\ell=\sum_{j=0}^{N-1}c_j\Phi_\tau(\ell_1/M_1-x_{j,1},\ldots,\ell_d/M_d-x_{j,d}),\quad 0\le\ell_r<M_r.$$
For $k\in\mathcal K=\prod_r\{-K_r,\ldots,K_r\}$ define the normalized grid DFT
$$\widetilde g_k=\frac1P\sum_{\ell_1=0}^{M_1-1}\cdots\sum_{\ell_d=0}^{M_d-1}g_\ell\exp\!\left(-2\pi i\sum_{r=1}^d k_r\ell_r/M_r\right).$$
Put $\widehat\Phi(m)=\prod_r\sqrt{\tau_r}\exp(-\pi\tau_r m_r^2)$. Then
$$\widetilde g_k=\sum_{q\in\mathbb Z^d}\widehat\Phi(k+q\odot M)\sum_{j=0}^{N-1}c_j\exp(-2\pi i(k+q\odot M)\cdot x_j),$$
where $(q\odot M)_r=q_rM_r$. In particular, $\widehat\Phi(k)>0$ and
$$\frac{\widetilde g_k}{\widehat\Phi(k)}=F_k+\sum_{q\ne0}\left[\prod_{r=1}^d\exp\!\left(-\pi\tau_r((k_r+q_rM_r)^2-k_r^2)\right)\right]\sum_{j=0}^{N-1}c_j\exp(-2\pi i(k+q\odot M)\cdot x_j).$$
For $s_r=\exp(-\pi\tau_rM_r(M_r-2K_r))\in(0,1)$ and
$$A=\prod_{r=1}^d\left(1+\frac{2s_r}{1-s_r}\right)-1,$$
the alias error satisfies
$$\left|\frac{\widetilde g_k}{\widehat\Phi(k)}-F_k\right|\le A\sum_{j=0}^{N-1}|c_j|.$$
alg-nufft-certified-gaussian-gridding-ty:
## Definition

Fix a dimension $d\ge1$, finite mode bounds $K_r\ge0$, a finite type-1 source list $(x_j,c_j)_{j<N}$ or type-2 data $(x_j)_{j<N},(f_k)_{k\in\mathcal K}$ as in [[def-nufft-transform-types-and-mode-conventions]], a nonempty finite ordered list of candidate tuples
$$\mathcal C=\bigl((\tau_r,M_r,w_r,L_r)_{r=1}^d\bigr)_{\nu=1}^C,$$
and an exact dyadic arithmetic format with precision $p\ge2$, exponent limits, elementary-series cap $J\ge1$, unit roundoff $u\le1/16$, and twiddle enclosure bound $0\le\epsilon_{\rm tw}\le1/4$. Source coordinates and coefficients are finite dyadics interpreted as exact real and complex inputs. Each candidate must have rational $\tau_r>0$, a power-of-two grid length $M_r=2^{q_r}$ with integer $q_r\ge0$, $M_r>2K_r$, integer width $w_r\ge1$ with $M_r\ge2w_r+1$, and integer image cutoff $L_r\ge1$. Reject malformed controls before arithmetic. Type 3 is not an input mode for this algorithm.

For each candidate in the supplied order, perform these finite steps; the first candidate that produces a complete interval certificate meeting the requested positive absolute tolerance is returned.

1. For each coordinate compute outward enclosures for
$$a_r=\frac{\pi}{\tau_rM_r^2},\quad s_r=\exp\!\bigl(-\pi\tau_rM_r(M_r-2K_r)\bigr),\quad d_r=\sqrt{\tau_r}\exp(-\pi\tau_rK_r^2),$$
$$S_r=\frac2{1-\exp(-a_r)},\quad T_r=2\exp(-a_rw_r^2)\left(1+\frac{1}{2a_rw_r}\right),\quad R_r=\frac{2\exp(-\pi L_r^2/\tau_r)}{1-\exp(-\pi L_r/\tau_r)}.$$
Use [[alg-certified-elementary-range-evaluation]] for all real exponential and square-root nodes, with $\pi$ enclosed by its Machin interval; use the outward interval operations for the rational DAGs. Set
$$A=\prod_{r=1}^d\left(1+\frac{2s_r}{1-s_r}\right)-1,\qquad T_d=\sum_{r=1}^dT_r\prod_{s\ne r}S_s,\qquad d_{\min}=\prod_{r=1}^d d_r.$$
Store outward upper bounds $A^+,T_d^+$ and a lower bound $d_{\min}^-$. If any required enclosure is non-finite, if a denominator interval in $A,S_r,T_r,R_r$ contains zero, if some $s_r$ enclosure is not strictly below $1$, or if $d_{\min}^-\le0$, reject this candidate as inconclusive; no division by an unverified multiplier is performed.

2. For each source-grid interaction retained by the periodic nearest-point rule
$$W_j=\prod_{r=1}^d\left\{\ell_r\in\mathbb Z/M_r\mathbb Z: \min_{n\in\mathbb Z}|\ell_r/M_r-x_{j,r}-n|\le w_r/M_r\right\},$$
reduce each exact dyadic displacement $\ell_r/M_r-x_{j,r}$ modulo one to $z_r\in[0,1)$. Enclose the one-dimensional kernel by evaluating the finite image sum
$$\sum_{n=-L_r}^{L_r}\exp\!\left(-\pi(z_r+n)^2/\tau_r\right)$$
with [[alg-certified-elementary-range-evaluation]], then add the symmetric interval with radius $R_r$ from step 1. All kernel and coefficient products and sums use outward interval arithmetic. For each grid cell $\ell$, this gives a complex rectangle enclosing its exact truncated-spread value $g_\ell$. Choose its lower-left corner $u_\ell$ as a dyadic center and an upward dyadic radius $e_\ell$ large enough to enclose $g_\ell-u_\ell$. Let $E_{\rm eval}$ be an outward upper bound for $(\sum_\ell e_\ell^2)^{1/2}$ and let $U$ be an outward upper bound for $\|u\|_2=(\sum_\ell|u_\ell|^2)^{1/2}$. Empty-source input returns the exact zero output and zero radii.

3. For either transform type, put $\eta=10u+\epsilon_{\rm tw}$, $\rho_r=(1+\eta)^{q_r}-1$ for each axis, and $\rho=\prod_r(1+\rho_r)-1$. For type 1, run the computed unitary radix-two FFT from [[alg-na-computed-unitary-radix-two-fft]] successively along grid axes $1,\ldots,d$, using a fixed lexicographic line order. Enlarge every computed unitary Fourier coordinate by the complex ball radius $\rho U$, then scale by $P^{-1/2}$, where $P=\prod_rM_r$. For each required mode evaluate the multiplier interval $d_k=\prod_r\sqrt{\tau_r}\exp(-\pi\tau_rk_r^2)$ with the same controls; if its lower endpoint is $\le0$, reject this candidate as inconclusive before division. Otherwise divide by that certified positive interval. Use outward complex-rectangle arithmetic. For each $k\in\mathcal K$, return the lower-left corner $z_k$ and an outward radius $r_k$ containing the resulting rectangle. Set
$$\epsilon_{\rm ana}=A^++\frac{T_d^+}{P\,d_{\min}^-},\qquad B_{\rm round}=\max_{k\in\mathcal K}r_k+ \frac{E_{\rm eval}}{\sqrt{P}\,d_{\min}^-}.$$
The returned error certificate is $\epsilon_{\rm ana}$ and $B_{\rm round}$.

4. For type 2, form the conjugate-transpose finite gridding factorization: for each input mode evaluate its multiplier interval and reject the candidate as inconclusive if its lower endpoint is $\le0$; otherwise divide by that positive interval. For the resulting mode rectangles choose lower-left dyadic centers $v_k$ and radii $e_k$ enclosing their deviations. Set $E_f$ to an outward upper bound for $(\sum_ke_k^2)^{1/2}$ and $V$ to an outward upper bound for $\|v\|_2$. Zero-fill the unused grid modes with zero centers and zero radii; apply the positive-sign unitary FFT on the same axes, and enlarge every computed output by radius $E_f+\rho V$. Scale by $P^{-1/2}$ and interpolate at each source point using the conjugate of the same truncated real Gaussian window, with outward complex-rectangle arithmetic at every operation. Return the lower-left corner $z_j$ and an outward radius $r_j$ containing each resulting rectangle; the type-2 rounding certificate is $B_{\rm round}^*=\max_jr_j$. Its analytic certificate is the same $\epsilon_{\rm ana}$ from step 3.

5. Enclose $\|c\|_1$ or $\|f\|_1$ from above by outward modulus and addition intervals. If every operation succeeds and the outward upper bound $\epsilon_{\rm ana}\|c\|_1+B_{\rm round}$ (type 1), or $\epsilon_{\rm ana}\|f\|_1+B_{\rm round}^*$ (type 2), is at most the requested tolerance, return the centers and their certificates with status certified. Otherwise continue to the next finite candidate. If no candidate succeeds, return inconclusive with the first unresolved interval, range, or FFT status; no error claim is made on this failure branch.

The analytic term consists only of the exact infinite-grid alias contribution and the omitted finite-spread tail. The reported rounding radius contains the finite image-series enclosure, outward arithmetic, and computed FFT error. The transform and FFT axes are fixed; a different normalization or sign convention is a different procedure.
thm-nufft-gaussian-gridding-error-and-ty:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice and the input hypotheses of [[alg-nufft-certified-gaussian-gridding-type1-type2]]. If $N=0$, the type-1 output is exactly zero and the type-2 output is empty, so their coordinatewise errors are zero. For $N>0$, fix a successful candidate with $P=\prod_rM_r$, exact multipliers $d_k=\prod_r\sqrt{\tau_r}\exp(-\pi\tau_rk_r^2)$, $d_{\min}=\prod_r\sqrt{\tau_r}\exp(-\pi\tau_rK_r^2)>0$, $s_r=\exp(-\pi\tau_rM_r(M_r-2K_r))$, and the exact spread-tail quantity $T_d$ of [[lem-nufft-gaussian-spread-truncation-tail]]. Put
$$\alpha=\prod_{r=1}^d\left(1+\frac{2s_r}{1-s_r}\right)-1,\qquad \epsilon_0=\alpha+\frac{T_d}{P d_{\min}}.$$
The algorithm returns an outward upper bound $\epsilon_{\rm ana}\ge\epsilon_0$.

For a type-1 output center array $\widehat F$ and its returned finite-arithmetic radius $B_{\rm round}$,
$$\|\widehat F-F\|_\infty\le\epsilon_{\rm ana}\|c\|_1+B_{\rm round}.$$
For the type-2 output center array $\widehat g$ and its returned radius $B_{\rm round}^*$,
$$\|\widehat g-A^*f\|_\infty\le\epsilon_{\rm ana}\|f\|_1+B_{\rm round}^*,$$
where $A_{k,j}=e^{-2\pi i k\cdot x_j}$ is the exact type-1 matrix and $A^*$ is its conjugate transpose.
When $N=0$, the type-2 output is empty and its coordinatewise assertion is vacuous; the procedure returns zero radius for this empty-output branch.

For fixed $d$, widths $w_r\le w$, image cutoffs $L_r\le L$, and fixed interval-series controls, one candidate's scalar grid/FFT/deconvolution work is
$$O\!\left(P\log P+N\prod_{r=1}^d(2w_r+1)\sum_{r=1}^d(2L_r+1)+|\mathcal K|\right).$$
Thus for bounded $w,L$ it is $O(P\log P+Nw^d)$, apart from the explicitly counted finite elementary-range evaluation work. No type-3 fast-cost claim follows.
ex-nufft-mri-fourier-samples:
## Statement

Consider a two-point object in $\mathbb T^2=[0,1)^2$ with locations
$$x_0=(1/4,0),\qquad x_1=(1/2,1/4),$$
and weights $c_0=1,c_1=2$. At the two type-3 frequency samples
$$\xi_0=(0,0),\qquad \xi_1=(1/3,1/5),$$
the exact nonuniform Fourier samples are
$$G_0=3,\qquad G_1=e^{-2\pi i/12}+2e^{-2\pi i(13/60)}.$$
These are finite Fourier samples of a point-source model of an MRI object; no acquisition or reconstruction claim is made.
ex-nufft-small-deconvolution-mode-is-inc:
## Statement

Use the dyadic format with precision $p=5$, exponent limits $e_{\min}=-2$, $e_{\max}=8$, unit roundoff $u=1/32$, elementary-series cap $J=64$, and twiddle bound $\epsilon_{\rm tw}=1/32$. Give the algorithm one type-1 source $x_0=0,c_0=1$, mode bound $K=7$, one candidate $\tau=1/40$, $M=16$, $w=L=1$, and requested positive absolute tolerance $1$. Its least positive subnormal is $\eta=2^{-6}=1/64$. The exact smallest deconvolution multiplier
$$d_{\min}=\sqrt{1/40}\,e^{-49\pi/40}$$
is positive but less than $\eta$. Therefore a finite outward dyadic lower endpoint for this multiplier cannot be positive, and the algorithm must reject the candidate as inconclusive at its positive-lower-bound check (or at an earlier range check); it cannot return a certified result using this candidate.
ex-nufft-clustered-sources-l1-error:
## Statement

Let $0<\delta<1/4$, take the one-dimensional type-1 data
$$x_0=1/4,\qquad x_1=1/4+\delta,\qquad c_0=1,\quad c_1=-1,$$
and include mode $k=1$. Then $\|c\|_1=2$ while
$$F_1=e^{-\pi i/2}(1-e^{-2\pi i\delta}),\qquad |F_1|\le2\pi\delta.$$
Thus this exact Fourier coefficient tends to zero as the source points cluster, although the coefficient l1 norm remains $2$. The successful-run theorem gives an absolute l1-scaled error certificate; this family has no positive lower bound on $|F_1|$ from which to infer a relative-error guarantee.
